text:
Maria G: Heads-up — marathon KV-cache regression popped on the long-context suite this morning. Memory steadily climbs after ~1.2M tokens and doesn't drop on expected eviction boundaries. Reproducer attached below.

AJ: ack. Can you paste the run args and the heap/profile snippet?

Maria G: Run args: `--workload long-context-interleaved --seq 16k --clients 8 --kv-policy auto`

Maria G: Heap snippet from perf/profile at 1.5M tokens: 
```
mem_total: 48GB
kv_cache_resident: 34.2GB
kv_extents_in_use: 7421
frag_ratio: 0.62
slow_evictions: 128
```

Sahil: Interesting — frag_ratio high. Did you run with the new kernel-selection heuristics landed last week? Those change pref thresholds and could affect per-request KV footprint.

Maria G: Yep, this build includes 2026-03 kernel-selection changes + batching tweak that increases continuous-batch windows. Suspect KV reuse patterns changed.

Lucy: @Maria G can you dump the `kv_hotset` timeline and the `batch_size_hist`? Want to see if sustained bigger batches are keeping hot KV alive longer and preventing timely compaction.

Maria G: Pasted `kv_hotset` (top lines):
```
[0s] hotset_pct=12
[300s] hotset_pct=28
[600s] hotset_pct=39
[1200s] hotset_pct=43
[1800s] hotset_pct=47
```
And `batch_size_hist`: `1: 22% | 2: 32% | 4: 30% | 8+: 16%`

AJ: That hotset climb looks correlated with the batch shift. If more requests fold into continuous batches, prefix hits keep entries in RAM as active and never age. Eviction won't trigger until thresholds hit.

Sahil: Two hypotheses: (1) the new kernel selection increases token-per-request kernels for long seqs, so each KV slot lives longer in active set; (2) batching heuristic extends window so a lot of tiny interleaved sessions form a pseudo-long session. Both cause memory growth.

Lucy: Proposed quick checks: (a) run with kernel-selection reverted, (b) force `batch.max_window=200ms` vs current `500ms`, (c) enable compaction sweep every 60s. We can A/B quickly in the bench harness.

Maria G: Running A/B now. Starting baseline (current build) run: `./bench --suite long-context-interleaved --seed 42`

ci-bot: baseline (2134567890-1) finished: peak_kv=34.2GB, frag_ratio=0.62, evictions=128, runtime=3h02m. See artifact: https://ci/redwood/jobs/2134567890-1

Maria G: Run (a) revert kernels -> started.

AJ: If revert fixes it, we need a reproable test in the regression harness before reintroducing kernel heuristics. The bench should include a metric: sustained_kv_growth_rate (GB per 100k tokens).

Sahil: Working on a small config that deterministically interleaves 512 long tails with random prefix hops to maximize frag. Patch: 
```
workload:
  sessions: 512
  tail_len: 8k
  interleave: true
  prefix_shuffle: 0.8
```
I'll push to `eng-runtime/bench-defs` and reference in the CI.

Maria G: Revert run finished: peak_kv=29.1GB, frag_ratio=0.44, evictions=94. Much better.

Lucy: Good signal. Next steps: (1) add the deterministic interleaved workload to the long-run suite, (2) add the sustained_kv_growth_rate metric and a threshold gate, (3) consider lowering default batch window for long-tail workloads or making it adaptive based on hotset growth.

AJ: Also add a telemetry counter for "kv_compaction_runs" and time-since-last-compaction. That helps correlate sweeps vs growth.

Sahil: I'll open a PR with the workload + metric and a failing CI test (expect growth_rate < 0.2GB/100k tokens).

Maria G: Thanks — filing an issue to track kernel-selection rollback implications: https://git/repo/issue/INF-4217. Tagging @Sahil @AJ @Lucy for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

Lucy: Nice triage. If the kernel heuristics are desirable for latency/cost, we should explore targeted fixes: compact-on-idle, smaller kv buckets for long sequences, or adaptive eviction thresholds. I'll sketch proposals in the issue.

ci-bot: benchmark AB run (2134567890-2) finished: revert_kernels: peak_kv=29.1GB, runtime=2h58m. artifact: https://ci/redwood/jobs/2134567890-2 :rocket:

AJ: Great. Let's not ship kernel-selection change to prod until we have the regen test and a mitigation. Meeting in 30 to decide rollout plan.

Maria G: On it — will add the bench PR and link artifacts in the issue.
